summary: Jens Schlieter works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1988–1999) and the University of Vienna (~1989–1990), and became Professor for Theory of Religion at the University of Bern around 2005.

Jens-Uwe Hartmann specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at LMU Munich, completed his habilitation at Göttingen, and received a doctorate from Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held professorships at Humboldt, FU Berlin, and LMU Munich.

Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Kim completed a PhD at SOAS University of London (~2005–2011), studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld specializes in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Oregon (~1968–1972) and Stanford University (~1970–1974), and held a position at Princeton University from approximately 2001 to 2018.

Jerzy Bańczerowski was a linguist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961). He served on the faculty at Adam Mickiewicz University from roughly 1961 to 2009, holding the title of professor from around 1970 to 2009.

Jessie Pons specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. She completed a doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University (~2005–2011) and served as Junior Professor in South Asian History of Religion at Ruhr University Bochum (~2016–2020).
Ji Hao is a Sinologist who completed a PhD at the University of Minnesota in 2013, supervised by Paul Rouzer in 2008. Hao held a post at the College of the Holy Cross around 2014.
Ji-yong Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who has served as a professor at Shitennoji University and Shitennoji Junior College.

Jiang Wu is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Nankai University and Harvard University under Tu Weiming, Robert M. Gimello, and Zhichao Chen. Since approximately 2002, he has served as a professor at the University of Arizona.
Jianjun Li works in the fields of philosophy and religious studies. Li earned a PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2011–2015) under the doctoral supervision of Michael von Brück.
Jianming Hu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and has served as a researcher at Komazawa University.

Jien Abe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1973) and served as a professor at Meiji University (~1982–2001), also holding an administrative post at the Eastern Institute.
Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teacher Hui Xian and earned an MA at Fo Guang University (~2011–2013) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi.
Jikai Fujiyoshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at Rissho University and was a member of Kyoto University.

Jikido Takasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned doctorates from Savitribai Phule Pune University and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo and Waseda, and served as president of Tsurumi University.
Jim G. Shaffer is an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Arizona State University and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1972).

Jim Rheingans specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After completing an MA at the University of Hamburg (~1998–2004), he earned his PhD (~2004–2008) through the University of the West of England and Bath Spa University under David P. Jackson.
Jim Taylor works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Macquarie University by 1989 and served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide.

Jin Y. Park specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Park held an appointment as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University around 2001 and has served as a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

Jin-il Chung works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Göttingen (~-1998) and held posts at the University of Göttingen and at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1994).
